articles.title: Iran and US trade attacks after Trump rejects report of Hormuz agreement | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Following US attacks near Bandar Abbas airport, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeted a US base in retaliation.  An unnamed US official said the US military shot down four Iranian attack drones and struck a ground control station. The ceasefire remains fragile as negotiations to end the war drag on, with both sides expressing confidence that they are not yet ready to collapse the agreement. Donald Trump rejected an Iranian report of a deal restoring commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz within a month, while Ebrahim Azizi, head of the Iranian parliament's national security committee, stated that Iran will not back down from its demands for uranium enrichment and sanctions relief.

articles.title: Oil prices jump after US launches new attacks on Iran
articles.rephrased_article: US forces conducted new airstrikes on Iran, targeting a military site in Bandar Abbas, a strategic port city. The attacks came despite a ceasefire between the two countries and raised oil prices globally. Brent crude rose by 3.75% to $97.83 (£73.15) per barrel, while US-traded crude was 4% higher at $92.22.  The strikes have escalated tensions in the region and threaten global energy supplies.

articles.title: Kaja Kallas warns against walking into Russian ‘trap’ as EU ministers meet for talks – Europe live | Europe | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kaja Kallas, the EU's foreign policy chief, warned against focusing on personalities in potential peace talks with Russia and urged the bloc to prioritize substance over individuals. She cautioned against falling into a Russian trap by discussing who would lead negotiations, emphasizing that the EU must be represented regardless of the chosen negotiator.  Several EU ministers are divided on appointing a single negotiator for Russia, with some advocating for a team effort while others prefer a more neutral approach. Péter Magyar, Hungary's new prime minister, is in Brussels to discuss frozen EU funds, but his visit has been overshadowed by ongoing negotiations over Orbán-era reforms.

articles.title: Mike Marshall: Meet Mike Marshall: The former soldier graduating at 69 after leaving school with no qualifications at 15 | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Mike Marshall, a 69-year-old former soldier and police officer, is graduating with a 2:1 in History from the University of East Anglia.  He left school at 15 without qualifications and pursued a career in public service before returning to education as a mature student. After an unexpected conversation with a university admissions staff member, Marshall enrolled and overcame initial challenges to achieve top grades. He plans to pursue a history-focused tour across Europe after graduation and considers further studies.  Marshall's journey exemplifies determination, lifelong learning, and second chances.

articles.title: Australia charges alleged ISIL-linked woman after return from Syria | ISIL/ISIS News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Australia has charged a 34-year-old woman with alleged links to the ISIL group after she returned from Syria. The woman faces charges of being a member of a "terrorist" organization and entering a declared conflict zone, potentially resulting in up to 10 years imprisonment. Police are investigating all adult returnees, including three women who face additional charges, including crimes against humanity.  The repatriation of these individuals follows the return of women and children from Syrian detention camps without trial.

articles.title: US firm fined for Australian immigration security failures. How much? Border force refuses to say | Australian immigration and asylum | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Australian Border Force (ABF) has penalized private prison company MTC, which runs Australian immigration detention centers, after a series of security failures including escapes and staff injuries. The ABF commissioner refused to disclose the financial penalties imposed on Secure Journeys, a subsidiary of MTC, citing commercial confidentiality. Senator David Shoebridge criticized the government's handling of the situation, questioning why details of the fines were being withheld from public view.  The investigation revealed numerous incidents, including detainees missing medical appointments due to staffing shortages and staff being hospitalized after attempting to rescue an unconscious detainee from a fire.

articles.title: What does NEET mean and why is Britain facing a ‘lost generation’ of 1.25m young people? | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Britain is facing a growing concern over the number of young people classified as "NEET," not in education, employment, or training. A review led by former Labour cabinet minister Alan Milburn warns that the number could rise by 25% to 1.25 million by early 2030s unless urgent action is taken. The report highlights a combination of fewer entry-level jobs, mental health challenges, and economic pressure as contributing factors to the increase in NEET levels. Business groups have also warned that higher employment costs are discouraging companies from hiring younger workers.

articles.title: US strikes Iran, drawing retaliatory attack on American base after Trump dismisses report of Hormuz deal - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard claimed responsibility for targeting a US airbase after the US military carried out strikes against Iranian drones near the Strait of Hormuz. The escalation in hostilities, which followed President Donald Trump's rejection of a report on a potential compromise deal with Tehran, heightened tensions and sent oil prices surging again.  The US official involved in the military operations stated that the actions were defensive and aimed at maintaining the ceasefire between the two countries.

articles.title: World Cup delegation compliant with US Ebola protocols, DR Congo says | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) football federation and FIFA confirmed that its World Cup delegation is compliant with US protocols related to the Ebola outbreak, clearing the way for the team to compete. The delegation has cancelled a training camp in Kinshasa and relocated preparations abroad, ensuring compliance with health and safety measures. DRC Ambassador to the US Yvette Kapinga Ngandu expressed confidence in the team's readiness and safety, while Sports Minister Didier Budimbu highlighted the government's efforts to ensure their preparedness for the tournament.

articles.title: US returns Palestinian rights expert Francesca Albanese to sanctions list | United Nations News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The United States government reinstated Francesca Albanese, a UN expert on Palestinian rights, to the sanctions list after a judge temporarily blocked the designation. The Trump administration had previously sanctioned Albanese for her criticism of Israeli policies and recommendations to the International Criminal Court (ICC).  Albanese's family filed a lawsuit against the sanctions, arguing they hindered her life and freedom of speech. A three-judge panel of the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit issued an administrative stay on the lower court injunction, allowing the government to reinstate the designation.

articles.title: Australia sues 3M over 'forever chemicals' in firefighting foam
articles.rephrased_article: Australia is suing 3M, a US manufacturing giant, for AU$2 billion in damages over the alleged use of toxic "forever chemicals" in firefighting foam that contaminated dozens of defense bases. The government claims 3M withheld information about the foam's environmental impact and misled them about its safety, despite knowing otherwise.  3M denies making PFAS in Australia and stopped selling the foam there 20 years ago.

articles.title: Lashkar-E-Taiba: LeT turns on its Pakistan masters over recognising Israel - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Saifullah Kasuri, deputy chief of Lashkar-e-Taiba, threatened Pakistan's frontline leadership and military officials with assassination if they recognized Israel, escalating tensions following President Trump's call for diplomatic ties.  Kasuri made these threats during a rally in response to the Abraham Accords, claiming no international power could coerce Muslim nations into accepting Israeli statehood. He emphasized Pakistan's growing defense alliance with Saudi Arabia as a countermeasure against Israeli influence and used inflammatory rhetoric about jihad and Palestine.

articles.title: Oil prices bounce higher after new US strikes on Iran - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Oil prices surged on Thursday, driven by renewed US strikes against Iran, erasing Wednesday's declines.  Iranian forces fired at four ships in the Strait of Hormuz, while Kuwait reported air defense responses to missile and drone attacks. Despite an Iranian official stating renewed hostilities were unlikely, US President Donald Trump threatened to "finish the job" if a peace deal wasn't reached. This volatile situation has led to mixed signals regarding the fragile ceasefire in the Middle East war, which continues to impact global energy markets. Asian stock markets mostly fell, with South Korean chipmaker SK hynix hitting a $1 trillion market capitalization.

articles.title: Australia charges woman who returned from Syria with joining Islamic State
articles.rephrased_article: Australia has charged a 34-year-old woman, identified as Rayann El Houli, with being a member of the terrorist organization Islamic State and entering a declared conflict zone.  The woman arrived in Australia last September after spending time in Syria's al-Hawl camp.  Hilda Sirec, federal police assistant commissioner, stated that all adult women who returned recently are under investigation.

articles.title: Oil Price Today (May 28): Crude oil surges nearly 3% after Iran says it targeted US airbase in retaliation for fresh American strikes - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards claimed responsibility for striking a US airbase, while US Central Command responded with strikes on an Iranian ground control station.  Oil prices surged as the situation escalated, with Brent crude reaching $97.29 per barrel and WTI crude at $91.71. Despite progress in negotiations between Washington and Tehran, uncertainty remains, leading to cautious responses from central banks. Analysts warn that even a deal may take months to normalize shipping activity through the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Strait Of Hormuz: 'War left regime desperate for cash': US sanctions authority overseeing Strait of Hormuz as Middle East conflict enters 90th day - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: The US administration imposed new sanctions on Iran’s Persian Gulf Strait Authority, targeting the agency overseeing shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The move comes after US forces carried out strikes on an Iranian military facility following the downing of Iranian attack drones.  Scott Bessent, US Treasury Secretary, stated that these sanctions are a result of Iran's desperate attempt to extort global maritime trade. Iran’s Revolutionary Guard defended the move, asserting that ships must follow designated routes through the waterway. The conflict has caused disruptions in oil and gas supplies, pushing prices up globally.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz says Youm-i-Takbeer symbolises Pakistan's strength, sovereignty and national unity - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Asif Ali Zardari both acknowledged the significance of May 28, 1998, as a defining moment in Pakistan's history. This day marked the successful completion of nuclear tests by Pakistan, which restored strategic balance in South Asia in response to India's nuclear ambitions.  The leaders praised the scientists, engineers, armed forces personnel, and workers who contributed to this historic achievement. They also highlighted Pakistan's commitment to national security and its right to self-defense while emphasizing the importance of unity and resilience in facing future challenges.

articles.title: US strikes Iran targets for second time in three days
articles.rephrased_article: The US military conducted new strikes on an Iranian military site in Bandar Abbas, a strategic port city. The strikes followed previous attacks on Iranian missile sites and boats in the Strait of Hormuz, which were also described as self-defense measures.  Iran condemned these actions as a violation of the ceasefire and vowed to retaliate. President Donald Trump stated that Iran is "negotiating on fumes" and threatened to resume a large-scale bombing campaign if an agreement is not reached.

articles.title: No specific port project identified, says Fiji’s Foreign Minister, day after Quad Foreign Ministers pledge assistance - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Fiji's Foreign Minister Sakiasi Ditoka stated that no specific port project has been agreed upon, despite a declaration by the Quad foreign ministers at their meeting in New Delhi.  The MCC Compact of the United States is being considered for funding feasibility studies on infrastructure development in Fiji. The announcement was made following discussions between the Quad countries and the Fijian government, which has been strengthening ties with China, particularly regarding infrastructure projects.

articles.title: Can the US and India repair ties over trade and China? | US-Israel war on Iran | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited India to repair strained ties following trade disputes and energy politics.  The trip comes amid a global energy crisis that has forced India to reconsider its oil and gas purchases, with Washington seeking to increase energy sales to the country. Both sides aim for a broader trade deal, but India's reliance on Russian crude and China's growing influence complicate the situation.

articles.title: Trump appears to threaten Oman over Strait of Hormuz impasse | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump threatened to use military force against Oman if it collaborates with Iran to control the Strait of Hormuz.  The US president's comments came after reports emerged of a potential memorandum of understanding between Iran and Oman that would grant them joint control over the waterway. Trump also reiterated his call for Arab countries, including Saudi Arabia and Qatar, to establish formal relations with Israel as part of any future US-Iran ceasefire agreement.  Critics condemned Trump's threat as reckless and a violation of international law.

articles.title: Trump threatens to ‘blow up’ Oman amid talks over strait of Hormuz | US foreign policy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump threatened to "blow up" Oman if it does not cooperate with the US in reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway that has been blocked by Iran since late February.  The US president made this statement during a cabinet meeting after reports emerged of talks between Iran and Oman regarding tolls for ships passing through the strait. Trump emphasized that the strait is international waters and will not be controlled by any single nation, but he also warned Oman that they must cooperate or face consequences.  Despite efforts to reach a peace deal with Iran, Trump's negotiations have stalled, leading to escalating tensions in the region.

articles.title: From Iran deal ultimatum to Ebola preparedness: Key takeaways from Donald Trump’s cabinet meeting - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump addressed a wide range of issues during a Cabinet meeting at the White House, including ongoing negotiations with Iran, tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, and domestic anti-fraud initiatives.  He expressed optimism about progress in talks with Tehran but warned that military action could resume if a deal is not reached. He also ruled out any arrangement allowing Iran or Oman to control the Strait of Hormuz, asserting US oversight. The President defended conditions at a New Jersey immigration detention facility while highlighting his administration's efforts to combat fraud and Ebola preparedness. Secretary of State Marco Rubio emphasized the administration's focus on protecting American citizens from the Ebola outbreak in Africa.

articles.title: Ghana welcomes first group fleeing South African anti-immigration protests | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Ghana welcomed its first group of 300 citizens evacuated from South Africa due to anti-immigration protests. The repatriation, facilitated by both countries' authorities, came after a wave of xenophobic attacks that saw campaigners demanding tighter controls on undocumented migrants.  Ghanaian officials described the evacuation as a voluntary process for those who felt unsafe in South Africa amidst rising tensions and violence against foreigners. South African authorities have condemned the violence and pledged to address it while also working with Ghana to ensure the safe return of its citizens.

articles.title: Why is Israel ramping up attacks in Lebanon despite a ceasefire? | Israel attacks Lebanon | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel is escalating its military operations in Lebanon, despite a US-brokered ceasefire. Iran has condemned these attacks and insists they must cease as part of any agreement with the United States.  US-Iran indirect talks continue while Israel intensifies strikes, killing and injuring dozens of people.

articles.title: Russia to task bankers with shooting down Ukrainian drones | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Russia has passed a bill allowing trained bank employees to shoot down Ukrainian drones. The legislation, which would see banks install electronic jamming systems and train staff to use them, aims to protect Bank of Russia facilities and other key institutions from drone attacks.  The bill must still be approved by the upper house Federation Council and signed by President Vladimir Putin before coming into force.

articles.title: India orders demolition drive along border as Pakistan tensions simmer | India-Pakistan Tensions News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: India's interior minister, Amit Shah, ordered the demolition of buildings within 15km of the border with Pakistan, citing the need to address "trans-border crimes" including infiltration and narcotics smuggling.  Shah also directed officials to enforce a zero-tolerance policy against illegal constructions along the border. This action comes amid heightened tensions between the two South Asian neighbors, following last year's deadly conflict in Kashmir.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Demolition of buildings near the border raises concerns about potential human rights violations.

articles.title: India sends emergency medical supplies for Ebola outbreak response in Congo - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: India has sent emergency pharmaceutical supplies to support the ongoing Ebola outbreak in Congo, as confirmed by the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention. The consignment includes essential diagnostics, therapeutics, infection prevention and control materials, and case management support.  The supplies were received in Uganda by the Eastern Africa Regional Coordinating Centre and will be deployed to affected communities in eastern DR Congo. The World Health Organization declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on May 17th.

articles.title: Iran government sells subsidised meat for Eid al-Adha under blockade | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's government is offering subsidized meat for Eid al-Adha, a significant religious holiday, to combat rising prices caused by US sanctions. The price of sacrificial meat has been set at 7.4 million rials ($4.30) per kilogramme, significantly lower than market rates. This initiative aims to control inflation and ensure access to meat during the holiday.  However, despite government efforts, many Iranians are facing economic hardship due to rising food prices and a weak currency.

articles.title: NASA just tested a thruster powerful enough for human missions to Mars | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory successfully tested a new magnetoplasmadynamic (MPD) thruster, achieving 120 kilowatts of power, marking a significant advancement in electric propulsion technology. This test surpasses the power output of current NASA thrusters and could pave the way for more efficient deep-space travel, including crewed missions to Mars. The MPD thruster's ability to generate sustained acceleration over long distances makes it a promising option for reducing mission duration and mitigating risks associated with prolonged spaceflight.

articles.title: EU states summon Russian envoys over Kyiv threat | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Several EU capitals, including Belgium and France, summoned Russian envoys to express anger over Moscow's warning for foreigners to leave Kyiv ahead of planned "systematic strikes."  The move comes after Russia issued a statement threatening foreign citizens in the city.  While President Vladimir Putin has said he is open to negotiations with Europe, many EU officials remain wary of engaging with Moscow due to its perceived lack of sincerity in peace talks. The spat is unlikely to smooth the way for the EU to mediate talks between Russia and Ukraine, but some European officials are considering taking up the role.

articles.title: Inside America’s hidden cave city where hundreds of children and families live off-grid inside sandstone cliffs | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Rockland Ranch, a self-sustaining community in Utah, is home to dozens of families living inside cave-like homes carved into sandstone cliffs. Founded by Robert Dean Foster in 1977, the settlement was designed as a remote haven for families practicing Mormon fundamentalism and operates largely independent of nearby towns. Residents rely on solar power, farming, livestock, and communal labor to support daily life. While many admire the community's self-reliance and communal lifestyle, others question its isolation and religious culture, particularly concerning polygamy and potential child welfare issues.  Despite controversy, Rockland Ranch continues to attract attention from photographers, filmmakers, and curious travelers.

articles.title: In pictures: Muslims across the world celebrate Eidul Azha - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Muslims around the world celebrated Eid al-Adha, also known as the Feast of Sacrifice, on Wednesday. The holiday marks the culmination of Hajj and commemorates Prophet Ibrahim's (AS) willingness to sacrifice his son to demonstrate obedience to Allah.  This year, the celebration takes place amidst heightened tensions between the US and Iran.

articles.title: ‘Eid does not enter tents’: Palestinians in Gaza face grim holiday | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Gaza residents are facing a somber Eid al-Adha, marked by the loss of loved ones and economic hardship caused by Israel's ongoing conflict. The traditional festivities, including visiting relatives, sharing meat sacrifices, and taking family photos, have been replaced with mourning for those killed in Israeli strikes. The Gaza Ministry of Health reports nearly 73,000 deaths since the conflict began.  Israel has imposed restrictions on movement and financial transfers, further exacerbating the economic crisis. The scarcity of livestock and soaring prices have led to a near-collapse of sacrificial animal projects, with many relying on frozen meat as an alternative. The Ru’ya charitable foundation, which previously slaughtered hundreds of animals annually, now distributes frozen meat to soften the impact of the absence of live sacrifices.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Plato: “The price good men pay for indifference to public affairs is...” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Plato's quote, "The price good men pay for indifference to public affairs is to be ruled by evil men," challenges the notion that stepping away from public discourse creates distance. The quote suggests that complete indifference can lead to consequences, even if individuals believe they are remaining neutral. While modern life presents constant information and opinions, many people experience feelings of disconnect due to overwhelming stimuli or personal concerns. Plato's message resonates today because it highlights the importance of awareness and participation in shaping society, regardless of individual involvement.

articles.title: Supreme Court upholds spouse’s right to joint posting - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court of Pakistan ruled that government employees covered under the wedlock policy have a legitimate expectation to be considered for joint postings unless compelling public interest dictates otherwise. The court overturned a lower tribunal's rejection of Naheeda Aziz's transfer request, citing federal and provincial governments' policies aimed at mitigating socio-economic hardships faced by married couples in government service due to different duty stations.  The court ordered the relevant authorities to reconsider her application within 15 days and emphasized that such beneficial policies should not be frustrated on technical grounds.

articles.title: US, Iran issue conflicting reports on deal as Trump says no sanction relief | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: US President Donald Trump and Iran have issued conflicting statements regarding a potential deal, with Trump stating that Iran will not receive sanctions relief and that the country's enriched uranium reserves will be destroyed.  Despite claims of Iranian surrender, Tehran has insisted on keeping its nuclear material. The US and Iran remain at odds over various issues including the continuation of sanctions against Iran, the blockade of Iranian ports, and control over the Strait of Hormuz. While a ceasefire was implemented in April, diplomatic efforts have stalled despite Trump's assertion that Iran is weakened and desperate to reach an agreement.  The White House has dismissed a report by Iran’s state TV claiming details of a deal, calling it a fabrication.

articles.title: Indian-Americans condemn Trump’s ‘racist’ post targeting Indians, Chinese: ‘Sends a dangerous message’ - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump shared a social media post on Truth Social that used derogatory language about Indians and Chinese people, prompting criticism from Indian-American lawmakers and advocacy groups.  The resolution introduced by Congressmen Raja Krishnamoorthi, Ted Lieu, and Pramila Jayapal condemned the president's amplification of the post, which attacked birthright citizenship and questioned the loyalty of immigrants. The controversy has been met with condemnation from community leaders who fear that this rhetoric could fuel anti-Asian hate.

articles.title: No feasts, no joy: Gazans mark a dark Eid - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Palestinian residents of Gaza face financial hardship and shortages this Eid al-Adha, casting a shadow over the holiday.  Prices for sacrificial sheep have skyrocketed due to limited supply and rising costs, making it impossible for many families to afford them. The United Nations reports that only one quarter of pre-war sheep remain in Gaza, while gas shortages make baking at home difficult. Despite a US-brokered ceasefire, Israeli air strikes continue, further impacting the lives of Gazans.

articles.title: Rescue teams find five of seven trapped in Laos cave | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Rescue teams in Laos have found five of the seven villagers trapped in a flooded cave for over a week. The quintet was discovered alive on Wednesday and are reported to be in good health. Thai volunteer rescuers joined the search effort, which included a diver who participated in the 2018 rescue of twelve boys and their coach from a flooded cave in northern Thailand.  The search continues for the remaining two missing individuals.

articles.title: Israeli military tells residents of swathe of southern Lebanon to leave | Lebanon | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Israel’s military has ordered residents in southern Lebanon to evacuate, escalating its offensive against Hezbollah. The IDF stated that all areas south of the Zahrani River are considered combat zones and will be targeted with force due to repeated violations of the ceasefire agreement by Hezbollah.  The US is attempting to broker a deal between Iran and the US, but the situation remains volatile.

articles.title: Viral fame spares ‘Donald Trump’ buffalo from Eid sacrifice in Bangladesh - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Bangladesh's Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed intervened to prevent the sacrifice of a rare albino buffalo, nicknamed "Donald Trump," after it was sold for Eidul Azha ritual slaughter. The nearly 700-kg animal had already been purchased by a buyer when authorities cited security concerns and public interest in its unusual appearance as reasons to spare it.  The Home Ministry ordered the buffalo be moved to the national zoo in Dhaka, refunded to the original buyer, and the farm owner, Ziauddin Mridha, will continue its care.

articles.title: Canada chooses Swedish early warning planes rather than US model | Business and Economy News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Canada has chosen to purchase a fleet of early warning planes from Sweden's Saab rather than a competing option from Boeing. Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that this decision aims to reduce reliance on the United States. The GlobalEye aircraft, based on the Bombardier Global 6500 jet, will be crucial for detecting and deterring threats in Canada's Arctic region.  The purchase is seen as a move towards diversifying from US military capabilities, aligning with Canada's commitment to strengthening ties with NATO allies like Sweden.

articles.title: Middle East crisis: Rubio says ‘some progress’ on US-Iran deal after Trump says ‘maybe we’ll just have to finish the job’ – as it happened | US-Israel war on Iran | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump suggested that a deal with Iran is still possible but threatened to "finish the job" if it's not satisfactory. Marco Rubio, his secretary of state, stated there has been "some progress" in talks but warned that other options are available if a deal isn't reached.  Trump also reiterated his red line regarding Iran's nuclear ambitions and doubled down on demands for more Arab countries to join the Abraham Accords. Trump claimed Iran is negotiating "on fumes" due to US sanctions, while Hegseth, Trump's defense secretary, argued that the blockade has crippled Iran's economy.  The White House dismissed an Iranian report of a framework deal as a fabrication, and Israel continued airstrikes in Lebanon despite a ceasefire.

articles.title: UK heatwave turns deadly: 9 die in separate water incidents over Bank Holiday weekend, urgent warning issued - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: At least nine people, mostly teenagers and children, have died in separate water-related incidents across the UK during the recent heatwave. The Royal Life Saving Society UK (RLSS UK) issued urgent warnings about the dangers of open water, emphasizing the risks associated with cold water shock.  Water safety experts are calling for immediate action to educate young people about these dangers before the summer holidays begin. Following the tragedies, drowning prevention organizations are demanding that schools start teaching water safety lessons immediately instead of waiting until September.

articles.title: UK will get no special treatment from EU, European ministers say | European Union | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: European ministers reaffirmed the established legal framework for the UK's future economic relationship with the EU, emphasizing that no cherry-picking of policies would be tolerated. The proposal for a single market for goods between the UK and the EU, which was rejected by officials, is seen as a radical departure from existing principles.  Despite this rejection, Maroš Šefčovič, the EU commissioner in charge of UK relations, stated that the EU remains united in its ambition to deepen ties with the UK while acknowledging the increasing constraints on progress due to the UK's red lines.

articles.title: DRC facing ‘catastrophic collision’ of Ebola and war, WHO chief warns | Ebola News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) chief, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, warned that the ongoing conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo is exacerbating an Ebola outbreak.  He stated that humanitarian access to affected areas is crucial for containing the virus and urged warring parties to agree to a ceasefire. The WHO has recorded at least 10 confirmed deaths and 220 suspected deaths from the outbreak, which has also spread to neighboring countries. Uganda's Health Ministry announced temporary border closures with the DRC to prevent further spread.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Conflict hinders Ebola response, risking a catastrophic outbreak.

articles.title: 'Greetings after 88 days': Iranians reconnect after 'world's longest internet shutdown' - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Iranians celebrated the end of a near-90-day internet shutdown imposed by authorities following nationwide protests and US-Israel strikes. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian issued an order to reopen international internet access, according to state media.  Keyumars, an Iranian computer programmer, reported that many businesses lost everything during the blackout due to its impact on social media use. Alireza Jafarzadeh, an Iranian editor, expressed joy over the restored connectivity, while Seyyid Sattar Hashemi, the Iranian Communications and Information Technology Minister, stated that the decision was in response to the people's desire for free communication.  However, internet access remains unstable and restricted, with platforms like WhatsApp still inaccessible without a VPN.

articles.title: ‘Put an end to this war’: Russian director Andrey Zvyagintsev makes new plea to Putin | Cannes film festival | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Andrey Zvyagintsev, acclaimed Russian director, sent a message to Vladimir Putin urging him to end the war in Ukraine.  Zvyagintsev's message, delivered through official channels, criticized the "senseless" war and called for an immediate ceasefire. Dmitry Peskov, Putin's spokesperson, rejected Zvyagintsev's appeal, claiming he had no right to criticize the war. The Kremlin has not responded to Zvyagintsev's message.

articles.title: The Baltics urgently need a de-escalation mechanism; Belarus can help | Russia-Ukraine war | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Baltic states, facing increasing drone incursions from Ukraine and Russia, are seeking de-escalation mechanisms to mitigate the risk of conflict. Belarus, a close ally of Russia, could play a crucial role in facilitating communication channels between the Baltics and Moscow.  These countries need a subregional security mechanism that prioritizes military de-escalation and avoids political posturing. The existing bilateral confidence-building agreements between Belarus and the Baltic states could serve as a framework for such a mechanism.

articles.title: Union Minister stresses need to advance space technology in India - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. Ram Mohan Naidu, Union Minister for Civil Aviation, emphasized the importance of advancing space technology in India during the launch of Mission STRATO-XI, a near-space demonstration conducted by Raudranex Space Technologies and Red Balloon Aerospace. The mission showcased India's first air-breathing cold plasma propulsion in the stratosphere.  The super-pressure balloon launched during the event could travel up to 25 km above earth, offering opportunities for research and testing across industries. Andhra Pradesh plans to develop a Space City at Sriharikota as part of its Aerospace and Defense Policy.

articles.title: Zelensky asked Trump for air defence munitions: AFP - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Volodymyr Zelensky, the President of Ukraine, has requested more ammunition for its Patriot air defense systems from the United States.  Zelensky emphasized that Ukraine relies almost entirely on the US for ballistic missile defense, highlighting the effectiveness of the Patriot systems in stopping Russian missiles. The request comes amidst strained relations between Ukraine and the US due to ongoing negotiations with Russia and a lack of progress towards a peace deal.

articles.title: Brexiters peddled ‘nationalistic pish’, said Reform UK’s Makerfield candidate | Makerfield byelection | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Reform UK candidate Robert Kenyon has sparked controversy with comments on a defunct rugby league forum criticizing Brexit and its proponents.  Kenyon, who is running against Labour's Andy Burnham in the Makerfield byelection, previously expressed skepticism about vaccines and Covid-19, backed Russia's invasion of Crimea, interacted with far-right figures, and made lewd remarks about Carol Vorderman. He now claims he voted for Brexit but has since become convinced it was a good decision despite its challenges.

articles.title: Meet Hana Khider: The woman leading an all-female team clearing ISIS landmines in Iraq where one wrong move means death | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Hana Khider, a Yazidi deminer, leads an all-female team clearing landmines and booby traps from villages in northern Iraq devastated by ISIS.  The work is dangerous as even a single mistake could trigger a deadly explosion. The documentary "Into the Fire," produced with The Nobel Prize and Grain Media, highlights Khider's mission and its impact on families seeking to return home after years of conflict. The film showcases how demining allows children to play safely, farmers to work their land, and communities to slowly rebuild daily life.  Khider's efforts are part of the International Campaign to Ban Landmines legacy, which received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1997 for its global anti-personnel mine elimination efforts.

articles.title: India orders demolition drive along Pakistan border - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Amit Shah, India's interior minister, ordered the demolition of illegal buildings within 15 kilometers of the Pakistan border.  He emphasized a zero-tolerance policy against such constructions and directed authorities to demolish all unauthorized structures. Shah also urged increased efforts to address infiltration, narcotics smuggling, encroachment, terror financing, and other trans-border crimes. This order was issued during a visit to Rajasthan, which borders Pakistan.

articles.title: Nearly half a million Russians killed in Ukraine war, UK spy chief says | Russia | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Anne Keast-Butler, chief of the GCHQ, estimated that nearly half a million Russian soldiers have been killed since the invasion of Ukraine began.  This estimate is higher than previous figures and reflects Russia's continued efforts to capture the eastern Donbas region, which has resulted in high casualty rates for the Russian military. The US Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, stated that 15,000 to 20,000 Russian soldiers are killed each month.  The GCHQ is working with its US counterpart, the National Security Agency, to develop security algorithms that can withstand attacks from quantum computers.

articles.title: Quote of the day by George Washington: “Be courteous to all, but intimate with few, and let those few be…” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: George Washington's quote, "Be courteous to all, but intimate with few, and let those few be well tried before you give them your confidence," emphasizes the importance of balancing openness and caution in relationships. The quote suggests that while courtesy is essential for respectful interactions, trust should be earned through consistent actions and observation over time.  This principle resonates today as technology facilitates constant connection but often fails to foster genuine intimacy.

articles.title: 'US-Iran peace deal could benefit entire region,' PM tells Pezeshkian in Eid call - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif spoke with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and expressed hope for a peace deal between Iran and the US.  He also spoke to Kuwait Crown Prince Sheikh Sabah Al Khaled Al Mubarak Al Sabah, who commended Pakistan's efforts in regional peace. Malaysian Prime Minister Dr Anwar Ibrahim acknowledged Pakistan's role in the ceasefire in the Gulf, highlighting the contributions of other countries. The leaders expressed solidarity with each other and their people during Eid celebrations.

articles.title: Canada to order military plane fleet from Sweden in shift from US suppliers | Canada | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Canada has chosen Saab’s GlobalEye early warning planes over a competing option from Boeing, marking a shift away from reliance on US defense firms. Prime Minister Mark Carney emphasized the importance of the decision for protecting Canada's vast Arctic territory, stating that it will allow for detection and deterrence of threats.  The purchase is expected to be worth six aircraft, with Saab planning to invest in research and development work in Canada as part of any deal.

articles.title: FIFA subpoenaed by New York, New Jersey in World Cup ticket investigation | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: FIFA has been subpoenaed by the states of New York and New Jersey as part of an investigation into ticket pricing and seat location accuracy for the 2026 World Cup. FIFA President Gianni Infantino defended the organization's pricing strategy, citing limited supply and demand.  The investigation seeks to address fan concerns about high prices and misleading information regarding seat locations. The states are seeking details on the general event pricing structure, location pricing structure, seat locations, and other relevant information related to the eight World Cup matches scheduled at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

articles.title: Elon Musk’s ex-girlfriend Ashley St Clair claims she was offered 'enough money equal to GDP of small nation' to not expose MAGA - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ashley St Clair, a former MAGA influencer and associate of Elon Musk, made explosive claims about the US political right, alleging coordinated private group chats involving senior figures and financial offers to stay silent. She also stated that she faced pressure from within the movement after distancing herself from MAGA politics.  St Clair has denied any personal gain from her experiences and plans to pursue a law degree to fight for change.

articles.title: Trump cabinet looks forward to progress on Iran deal in 'coming hours, days' - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump and his cabinet discussed the ongoing negotiations with Iran, stating they are "not satisfied" with the deal's terms but will reach an agreement.  Secretary of State Marco Rubio emphasized that diplomacy is the first option, while US War Secretary Pete Hegseth highlighted the economic struggles in Iran. The meeting focused on a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) aimed at preserving the ceasefire and addressing regional security issues. However, Iranian state TV reported on a draft agreement outlining Iran's restoration of commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, while the US refuted these claims.  The negotiations have slowed down due to disagreements over wording, raising concerns about the fragile ceasefire and potential for escalation in the region.

articles.title: Donald Trump says US 'not satisfied' with Iran deal yet
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump stated he is "not satisfied" with the terms of the ongoing negotiations with Iran, despite acknowledging Tehran's desire to reach an agreement.  The White House dismissed reports of a draft deal as a "complete fabrication", while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed optimism about progress, but declined to provide specifics on disagreements between the two sides. The US and Israel have conducted strikes against Iran since February 28th, sparking conflict in the region, with both sides continuing to claim self-defense.

articles.title: US building Ebola quarantine center in Kenya for Americans amid outbreak | Trump administration | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The Trump administration is establishing a quarantine and treatment center in Kenya for Americans affected by the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The facility will provide access to high-quality care, including critical care needs, but further transport for more advanced care may be considered. Jennifer Nuzzo, an epidemiologist and director of the Pandemic Center at Brown University School of Public Health, expressed concerns about the ethical implications of this approach, arguing that it could hinder the virus's containment efforts and discourage Americans from disclosing their exposure.  Jeremy Konyndyk, president of Refugees International and former executive director of the USAID Covid-19 taskforce, also criticized the decision, stating that it discourages health workers from volunteering in the effort to contain the outbreak.

articles.title: What is the Lobito Corridor, cited by US Africa envoy as model for ties? | International Trade News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Frank Garcia, the newly appointed assistant secretary of state for African affairs, highlighted the Lobito Corridor as a model for US trade and investment in Africa. This strategic rail route connects Angola's port of Lobito to mineral-rich regions of the DRC and Zambia.  Supporters view it as a means to boost regional trade, create jobs, and improve infrastructure while offering investment opportunities. Critics argue that the project primarily serves US efforts to secure alternative supply chains for critical minerals needed for clean energy technologies and defense, potentially exacerbating conflicts in Africa. The Lobito Corridor faces concerns about displacement of communities, environmental impacts, and potential human rights abuses.  The project has drawn criticism from organizations like Global Witness and the United Nations, which have raised concerns about its alignment with US strategic interests and its impact on vulnerable populations.

articles.title: Thrice rebuffed for US visa, Sanjay Mehrotra joins Satya Nadella and Sundar Pichai in the trillion-dollar club - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Sanjay Mehrotra, CEO of Micron Technology, achieved a remarkable rise from being denied a student visa in the 1970s to becoming one of America's most valuable technology company leaders.  His journey exemplifies an extraordinary trend: three of the world’s most valuable technology companies – Microsoft, Alphabet, and Micron – are now run by Indian-born executives who arrived in the US as middle-class strivers. This success story is reshaping Silicon Valley and the political debate over globalization in Donald Trump's MAGA-fied America.  Mehrotra's rise also highlights a shift in corporate America towards technocratic immigrant executives with deep managerial discipline, fueled by the AI era's demand for operational complexity and geopolitical balancing.

articles.title: Hundreds flee India migrant crackdown towards Bangladesh - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Hundreds of people in India's border region with Bangladesh have fled to the frontier after the Indian government ordered the construction of detention centers for undocumented Bangladeshi migrants and Rohingya refugees.  Prime Minister Narendra Modi, leading the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), has implemented a hardline policy to "detect, delete, and deport" illegal migrants, citing national security concerns. The decision has fueled anxiety among India's Muslim population, with some fearing increased marginalization. Home Minister Amit Shah announced the formation of a special committee on demographic change, emphasizing the threat posed by illegal migration to national security.

articles.title: India seeks proposals for 5th generation combat jets: ANI - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: India has invited proposals from three Indian companies to locally manufacture a fifth-generation combat aircraft. The shortlisted bidders are Tata Advanced Systems, joint ventures between Larsen and Toubro-Bharat Electronics, and Bharat Forge-BEML.  The program aims to bolster the Indian Air Force, which currently operates below its approved strength of 42 squadrons. This initiative aligns with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s goal of boosting local manufacturing and enhancing India's military capabilities.

articles.title: Why is Israel attacking Lebanon’s Nabatieh, the major southern city? | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel has intensified its attacks on Lebanon, targeting the southern city of Nabatieh.  The Israeli military ordered the forced displacement of the population and hit the city with artillery shelling.  Hezbollah responded with strikes against advancing Israeli forces. The attacks come amidst ongoing negotiations between Lebanon’s government and Israel, which have been stalled by continued violence.  Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared a "war" on Hezbollah, while the city of Nabatieh has been repeatedly targeted since 1978.  The conflict has displaced over 1.2 million people in Lebanon.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Forced displacement and artillery shelling of civilians are serious human rights violations.

articles.title: Trump Board of Peace's official Gaza fund is empty - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump’s Board of Peace, established to rebuild Gaza after a ceasefire agreement, has received no funding despite pledges from member countries.  The board's fund, administered by the World Bank and endorsed by the United Nations, is designed for the reconstruction and development phase which has not yet been reached. Vladimir Putin and other international leaders have been invited to participate in the board but it has faced criticism for its lack of transparency and alignment with traditional Middle East diplomacy.  The US pledged $10 billion to the board while Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates each promised at least $1 billion.

articles.title: South Korea detains dissident who fled China in rubber boat
articles.rephrased_article: Dong Guangping, a former Chinese police officer and human rights activist, was detained in South Korea after fleeing China on a rubber boat.  He had spent over 30 hours at sea before being rescued by the Korean coast guard. Human Rights in China (HRIC) urged Seoul to uphold his humanitarian rights and allow him asylum or safe passage to Canada where his family resides. This is not the first time Dong has attempted to escape China, having been deported back multiple times after previous attempts.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz extends Eid greetings to armed forces chiefs, pays tribute to on-duty personnel - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif extended Eid greetings to the Chief of Defence Forces, Field Marshal Asim Munir, and other senior military officials. The prime minister praised the armed forces' professionalism and sacrifices for national security, expressing gratitude for their service.  Munir and the services chiefs reciprocated the sentiment, reaffirming the armed forces' commitment to Pakistan's defense.

articles.title: Ghana welcomes Pope Leo XIV's apology over Catholic Church's role in slavery
articles.rephrased_article: Ghana welcomed Pope Leo XIV's apology for the Catholic Church's role in slavery, describing it as an important step towards healing and reconciliation. The Pope acknowledged the Church's involvement in legitimizing slavery and its historical response to requests from rulers that included "regulating and legitimising forms of subjugation."  The country's government stated that the apology reinforced global understanding of confronting historical injustices and called for truth-telling, moral responsibility, and justice. Human Rights Watch emphasized that while the apology was significant, real reparative justice requires action from religious institutions, states, and corporations that benefited from slavery.

articles.title: Mogadishu gathers for Eid with prayers, family meals and outings | Religion News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Muslims in Mogadishu, Somalia celebrated Eid al-Adha, the Festival of Sacrifice, with communal prayers, family meals, and outings. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud addressed the gathering at the Islamic Solidarity Mosque, highlighting improvements in security since 2006.  The holiday traditionally involves a ritual sacrifice of livestock, which is shared among those in need to reflect the festival's emphasis on charity and community. The celebration comes amidst ongoing challenges including drought, famine risk, and political instability.

articles.title: Trump calls full cabinet meeting amid negotiation slowdown with Iran - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump will hold a cabinet meeting at the White House on Wednesday amid growing tensions in the Middle East and ongoing negotiations with Iran over a possible agreement aimed at reducing regional conflict. The meeting comes after weeks of indirect talks, which have slowed recently due to disagreements over wording.  Diplomats say most of the proposed Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) has already been agreed upon, but Iranian state TV reported on an alleged framework that includes Iran restoring commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the US withdrawing military forces from Iran’s vicinity. The White House denies these reports, calling them a fabrication.

articles.title: Israel orders evacuation of Lebanese city as Hezbollah conflict escalates
articles.rephrased_article: Israel has ordered the evacuation of the southern Lebanese city of Tyre following air strikes on Hezbollah, an Iran-backed armed group, which it claims is violating a US-brokered ceasefire.  Hezbollah retaliated by attacking Israeli troops and civilians, prompting Israel's prime minister to announce an expansion of ground operations. The escalation threatens to derail peace talks between the US, Israel, and Iran, with Lebanon drawn into the conflict since March 2nd after Hezbollah launched rockets into Israel in retaliation for an Israeli strike on Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Khamenei.

articles.title: WHO chief calls for DRC ceasefire to tackle Ebola outbreak | Democratic Republic of the Congo | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO director, called for an immediate ceasefire in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo to combat the Ebola outbreak.  The outbreak has spread to Uganda, with seven confirmed cases and one death reported there. The WHO recommends against border closures as they can increase informal crossings and hinder disease monitoring. The response to the outbreak is complicated by ongoing conflict, displacement, attacks on health facilities, and challenges in accessing communities.

articles.title: Ed Husic calls on Labor to establish ‘red line’ on Israel’s actions, including treatment of flotilla activists | Australian foreign policy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Labor MP Ed Husic called for a "red line" from Australia's government, including tougher sanctions, an end to defense cooperation and a block on supplying parts for the F-35 fighter jet. Husic expressed concern about Israel's actions, citing mistreatment of activists, the death of Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom, and destruction of Australian war graves. Penny Wong, the foreign minister, has condemned Israel's actions while Anthony Albanese and other MPs have called for a tougher response to what they see as unacceptable behavior from the Israeli government.

articles.title: Haj pilgrims stone the devil in final ritual - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Muslim faithful participated in the annual Haj pilgrimage, symbolically stoning pillars representing the devil near Makkah.  Over 1.7 million pilgrims are taking part this year, with the event overshadowed by the ongoing US-Israeli conflict with Iran. The Haj, which involves a series of outdoor rituals over several days, is being held during intense heat.

articles.title: Five people found alive after week trapped in flooded Laos cave
articles.rephrased_article: Five villagers trapped in a flooded cave in Laos for a week have been rescued. Lao and Thai rescue teams worked together to locate the group, who had entered the cave seeking gold deposits and wildlife.  Two other villagers remain missing, and rescuers are continuing their search.

articles.title: CDF Munir spends Eidul Azha with frontline troops in Zhob, says brutal acts cannot weaken nation’s resolve - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Field Marshal Asim Munir, Chief of Defence Forces, visited frontline troops in Balochistan's Zhob during Eidul Azha.  He expressed solidarity with the troops and condemned the Quetta train bombing that killed 14 people on Sunday. Munir emphasized the unwavering resolve of the armed forces and vowed to continue fighting terrorism with full force. He also paid tribute to the sacrifices made by soldiers and martyrs in defense of Pakistan. The military leadership extended Eidul Azha greetings, reaffirming their commitment to defending national sovereignty and achieving lasting peace.

articles.title: Ebola-hit DR Congo faces 'catastrophic collision' of disease and conflict, WHO warns
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) has warned that the ongoing conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo is hampering efforts to control a devastating Ebola outbreak.  Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO director-general, stated that humanitarian access is crucial for containing the virus and called for an immediate ceasefire. The outbreak, which began in Ituri province, has resulted in 220 suspected deaths and challenges such as poor road conditions, mass displacement, and attacks on health facilities are hindering response efforts.  The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) is increasing its presence to support the fight against the virus.

articles.title: Five villagers found alive in Laos cave as search continues for two missing | Laos | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Five villagers trapped in a flooded cave in central Laos for over a week have been found alive, with five rescued and two still missing. Rescue Volunteer for People, a Lao organization working alongside local authorities, confirmed the discovery after divers located the trapped individuals.  The rescue operation involved teams from Thailand and other nations who had experience rescuing people from similar situations, including the 2018 Thai cave rescue of 12 schoolboys and their coach. The villagers entered the cave in May, but heavy rain triggered flash flooding that blocked the exit.

articles.title: Billionaire wars: Jeff Bezos steals $230M Moon deal from Elon Musk as NASA selects Blue Origin for the first of three uncrewed lunar missions | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: NASA announced the selection of Blue Origin, a company founded by Jeff Bezos, to carry out the first in a planned series of three uncrewed lunar missions. The $230 million contract will see Blue Origin's Blue Moon cargo lander transport scientific payloads and test technologies near the Moon's south pole. This decision marks a symbolic win for Bezos in his ongoing rivalry with Elon Musk, whose company, SpaceX, remains deeply involved in NASA's Artemis program. The missions are part of NASA's effort to create an operational lunar base by the next decade and will help test technologies needed for future astronaut operations on the Moon.

articles.title: Chemical tank rupture in Washington state causes one death, multiple injuries - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A chemical tank at a Nippon Dynawave Packaging facility in Longview, Washington ruptured on Tuesday morning, resulting in one fatality and nine injuries. The injured include eight employees and one firefighter who was treated and released from the hospital. Governor Bob Ferguson offered condolences to those affected by this tragedy.

articles.title: How badly is Europe affected by fertiliser shortages due to the Iran war? | Food News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The European Union is launching a new Fertiliser Action Plan to address disruptions caused by the war in Iran and the Strait of Hormuz. The plan includes emergency financial support for farmers, increased imports from other countries, and measures to boost domestic production. While Europe's reliance on Gulf supplies is less than some regions, rising fertiliser prices due to the disruption are impacting food production costs and competitiveness.  The EU acknowledges that these challenges could lead to a backlash against green policies in rural areas as right-wing and populist parties gain ground.

articles.title: AI-Guided Cruise Missiles: 'Special mission warhead': North Korea tests AI-guided cruise missiles, ballistic rockets near South Korea | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: North Korea conducted a series of missile tests, including tactical ballistic missiles, artillery rockets, and AI-guided cruise missiles, near South Korea. Kim Jong Un, leader of North Korea, stated that these weapons will be deployed near the border with South Korea, equipped with precision navigation and AI-guided control capable of striking targets at 100 km (62 miles).

articles.title: Israel claims it killed new Hamas armed wing chief in Gaza strike - World - DAWN.COM

articles.title: Elon Musk’s Starlink comes to air travel: American Airlines to transform in-flight internet experience by 2027 | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: American Airlines is investing in Starlink's satellite internet system for its narrowbody fleet, aiming to provide faster and more reliable in-flight Wi-Fi starting in early 2027. The rollout will involve over 500 aircraft, including Airbus A321neo and A321XLR models, marking a shift from the traditional patchy connectivity often experienced on flights.  This move reflects changing passenger expectations for seamless digital experiences during travel, positioning airlines to compete based on in-flight Wi-Fi quality rather than just seat pitch or food options.

articles.title: FM Dar assures UN chief of Pakistan's 'continued engagement and dialogue' to restore peace in region - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Ishaq Dar, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, met with António Guterres, the UN Secretary-General, in New York to discuss regional developments. Dar emphasized the importance of a peaceful and stable Afghanistan for regional security and reaffirmed Pakistan's commitment to international law and UN principles.  He also addressed Palestine and the need for a two-state solution.

articles.title: Elon Musk’s Starlink comes to air travel: American Airlines to transform in-flight internet experience by 2027 | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: American Airlines is partnering with Starlink, a satellite internet provider, to upgrade its in-flight Wi-Fi for more than 500 narrowbody aircraft. The rollout, beginning in early 2027, aims to provide speeds closer to home broadband and eliminate the frustrating buffering and lag experienced by passengers on traditional aircraft connections. This shift reflects a growing trend among airlines to prioritize reliable connectivity as a key factor in passenger choice.

articles.title: Armed forces reaffirm commitment to peace and national unity on Eidul Azha - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Pakistan armed forces, led by Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf, and Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu, extended Eidul Azha greetings to the nation. The military leadership expressed gratitude for the sacrifices made by martyrs, security personnel, law enforcement agencies, and citizens in safeguarding the country. They also prayed for lasting peace, prosperity, and national unity while acknowledging the resilience of the Pakistani people.

articles.title: Dissident detained in South Korea after fleeing China in rubber boat | China | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A 68-year-old Chinese dissident, Dong Guangping, was apprehended by South Korean coast guard after attempting to flee China in a rubber boat.  He had previously attempted to escape multiple times, including being deported back to China from Thailand and Vietnam. Zang Xihong, a Chinese dissident in Canada, has been in contact with Dong since 2015 and confirmed his determination to leave China despite previous failures.  The distance between Weifang, China, and Taean, South Korea, is over 300km.

articles.title: First Ghanaians set to be repatriated from South Africa over anti-immigrant protests
articles.rephrased_article: Ghanaian authorities are repatriating the first group of 800 citizens registered to leave South Africa, following a wave of anti-immigrant protests. The repatriation effort began Wednesday morning with dozens of buses chartered by the Ghanaian embassy dropping off passengers at Johannesburg's OR Tambo airport.  The remaining registered citizens will be screened and depart later, according to Ghanaian High Commissioner Benjamin Quashie. March and March, a citizen-led movement for immigration reform, has organized protests demanding illegal immigrants leave the country by June 30th. The protests have sparked concerns about potential violence as some fear the deadline could lead to xenophobic attacks.

articles.title: New airline South Air operates trial flight to Gwadar - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: South Air, a private airline, launched its first trial flight service from Karachi to Gwadar, marking a significant step towards improved air travel facilities in the coastal region. The new air service is anticipated to reduce travel time between Gwadar, Karachi, Quetta, and other cities while boosting trade, tourism, and development activities across the Makran division.

articles.title: Iran war live: Israel kills 31 in Lebanon; Tehran blasts US truce violation | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel intensified its attacks in southern Lebanon, killing 31 people and injuring 40 others on Tuesday. articles.title: One person killed in latest US military strike on alleged drug boat in Pacific | US military | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US military conducted another strike on a suspected drug vessel in the eastern Pacific, resulting in one fatality and two survivors. articles.title: Brazil’s Flavio Bolsonaro meets with Trump amid troubled presidential bid | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro, met with US President Donald Trump at the White House. articles.title: Three killed in Israeli strike on Gaza City, medics and witnesses say
articles.rephrased_article: Israeli forces carried out a major air strike on a residential building in Gaza City, killing at least three Palestinians and injuring dozens more. The attack targeted Mohammed Odeh, the commander of Hamas's armed wing, according to Israel's Prime Minister's office.  Rescue teams struggled to reach the upper floors due to the scale of the damage and congestion. This latest strike comes despite a ceasefire being in place since October 10th, with both Hamas and Israel accusing each other of breaching the agreement. The attack follows a series of deadly Israeli strikes on Gaza, raising concerns about the fragile peace process.

articles.title: Storied New York food co-op votes to boycott Israeli products after contentious campaign | New York | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Members of the Park Slope Food Coop in Brooklyn voted to boycott approximately a dozen products from Israel and Israeli settlements in occupied Palestine, marking the culmination of years of debate over the conflict. articles.title: The judiciary’s role in complete justice - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court of India has ruled that safe travel on National Highways is a fundamental right, declaring it an integral part of the Right to Life under Article 21. The government aims to reduce road accident fatalities by 50% by 2030 and has adopted a strategy focusing on education, engineering, enforcement, and emergency medical services. Despite the decrease in fatalities, the issue remains concerning, prompting the court's intervention under Article 142 of the Constitution which allows for complete justice even when existing laws are insufficient.

articles.title: Iran vows not to let aggression go unanswered after US violates truce - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Iran accused the United States of violating a ceasefire by targeting its missile sites and mine-laying boats. Iran has threatened retaliation and warned against any further US or Israeli air strikes on its territory. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump is holding a cabinet meeting at Camp David as talks between Iran and the US approach a critical point.

articles.title: Group of women and children with alleged ISIL ties returns to Australia | ISIL/ISIS News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Australian Federal Police have not made any arrests but are continuing investigations into a group of 19 women and children who returned to Australia from a Syrian refugee camp.
